paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Israel lost a battle and the elders asked a good question: "Why has the LORD brought defeat on us before the Philistines today?" (1 Samuel 4:3). Then they skipped past the answer and went straight to a plan. They figured if they carried the ark of the covenant into camp, it would "save us from the hand of our enemies" (1 Samuel 4:3). That's like me grabbing a fancy new timer and thinking it will bake the cookies FOR me.

The ark was real and it was holy. But the text never says the LORD told them to bring it to the battle. The shout was loud enough to shake the ground, and Israel still fell, and the ark was captured (1 Samuel 4:5, 10, 11). I think that's the lesson, baker. Having God's things near you is not the same as having God's heart, and a loud shout can't take the place of a real answer to a real question.

This is a heavy chapter, and I'm not going to joke my way past it. Eli's heart trembled for the ark, and Phinehas's wife named her son Ichabod, saying "The glory has departed from Israel" (1 Samuel 4:13, 21). So ask yourself the elders' question, but stay with it long enough to listen. Don't run to a plan before you ask what God is saying to you. And keep your apron on, because this story is not over yet.
